textbookText: Covalent bonding. Covalent Bond : The bond which is formed between two or more atoms of the same or different elements by equal sharing of electron between any two combining atom is known as covalent bond. It may be polar or non polar. It is denoted by dash line (—).
Types of covalent bond: Depending up on the number of electrons are shared. There are types of covalent bond.
Single covalent bond: It is formed by the sharing of one electron between the two combining atoms. Example: H2, F2 etc.
Double covalent bond: It is formed by the sharing of two electrons o==o between the two combining atoms. Example: 02, C02 etc.
Triple covalent bond: It is formed by the sharing of three electrons NE-N between two combining atoms. N2, C2H2 etc.

89. Resonance

Some molecules cannot be represented by a single Lewis structure. Two or more electronic structures of equivalent energy are '.vritten for such molecules. The actual structure is regarded as a contribution of these various structures. Such phenomenon is called resonance. It is defined as the electronic effect vvhich arises due to delocalization of pie (ft) electron i.e. the electron of a multiple bond and lone pair of electron. Due to this effect, a molecule can be written in two or more electronic structure. Such electronic structures are called resonance or canonical structure and these structures are inter convertible to each other, none of these structure is a true of stable structure. Hence, the actual structure is regarded as a hybrid of all these canonical form, called resonance hybrid. It is denoted by a straight double headed arrow (++). Example:
